ground_truth.unit: percentage points (party-list turnout, % of registered voters)
ground_truth.context: Table 1 ("Intention-to-Treat Effect on Electoral Returns at the Barangay Level"), column 1.  Intention-to-treat effect of random assignment of a town-hall (deliberative) campaign by either party list (Akbayan or Umalab Ka) on party-list turnout, as a percentage of registered voters, from official COMELEC returns of the May 2013 party-list election, across all experimental barangays (one assigned treatment and two controls per selected municipality). Regression of the electoral return on the assignment dummy with municipality (city) fixed effects (equation 1); inference under randomization of the treatment, permutation p-value p = .404.  Not significant.

ground_truth.unit: percentage points (vote share of the treating party list)
ground_truth.context: Table 1, column 2: intention-to-treat effect of town-hall-meeting assignment on the vote share (% of total party-list votes) of the party list campaigning in the barangay, Akbayan and Umalab Ka pooled; all experimental barangays; same specification as column 1 (assignment dummy, municipality fixed effects, randomization inference, permutation p = .048).  The paper's headline result.

Table 1, column 3: intention-to-treat effect on Akbayan's vote share (% of party-list votes), barangays of the municipalities randomly assigned to Akbayan only; assignment dummy with municipality fixed effects, randomization inference (permutation p = .087).

Table 1, column 4: intention-to-treat effect on Umalab Ka's vote share (% of party-list votes), barangays of the municipalities randomly assigned to Umalab Ka only; assignment dummy with municipality fixed effects, randomization inference (permutation p = .141).  Not significant.
Number of barangays (all experimental barangays, both party lists) in the turnout and pooled vote-share regressions of Table 1, columns 1 and 2.
Number of barangays in the Akbayan vote-share regression, Table 1 column 3 (barangays of the Akbayan municipalities).
Number of barangays in the Umalab Ka vote-share regression, Table 1 column 4 (barangays of the Umalab Ka municipalities).

ground_truth.location: SI Table C.3, Akbayan Treatment panel, column 1 (Index), ITT row
ground_truth.context: Supporting-information Table C.3 ("Intention to Treat Effect on Attitudes on Poverty"), upper panel (Akbayan treatment), column 1. Post-election survey respondents in the Akbayan municipalities. Outcome: the summary index of poverty-related attitudes (Anderson 2008: the four items Poverty, Gap, CCT and Corruption, each oriented so higher means more agreement, standardized with respect to the control group's mean and s.d., combined as an inverse-covariance weighted average).  Linear regression on treatment assignment with city fixed effects (equation 3), weighted to adjust for the oversampling of meeting attendees (inverse probability weights: the proportion of self-reported attendees in the survey relative to actual attendees from the meetings' attendance sheets, in treatment barangays), standard errors clustered by barangay (p = 0.017).  The surveyed municipalities exclude Imus, Pateros and Santa Maria.  The main text shows this estimate in Figure 5.

i4r.notes: Team-level verdict (code reproduces the paper's output).  Database row "appendix table c.3" (o_coeff 0.496, o_p 0.017) is the remove-weights robustness check: r_coeff 0.138 (SE 0.160, p = 0.391), not transcribed.

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=0.33706 vs claimed=0.496 (relative error 32.04%, tolerance 2.00%).

ground_truth.location: SI Table C.3, Umalab Ka Treatment panel, column 1 (Index), ITT row
ground_truth.context: SI Table C.3, lower panel (Umalab Ka treatment), column 1: the same poverty-attitudes summary index and specification as the Akbayan panel (assignment, city fixed effects, attendance weights, clustering by barangay), respondents in the Umalab Ka municipalities (p = 0.048).  The text reports it as "a small, but significant ITT" on the poverty index (Figure 5, lower panel).

i4r.notes: Team-level verdict.  Database row "appendix table c.3" (o_coeff 0.126, o_p 0.048), remove weights: r_coeff 0.182 (SE 0.183, p = 0.321), not transcribed.

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=0.319969 vs claimed=0.126 (relative error 153.94%, tolerance 2.00%).

ground_truth.location: SI Table C.4, Akbayan Treatment panel, column 1 (Index), ITT row
ground_truth.context: SI Table C.4 ("ITT Effect and CACE on Attitudes on Gender"), Akbayan treatment panel, column 1.  Outcome: the summary index of attitudes on gender discrimination and sexism built from the five gender items (Female Rep., Female Pol., Equality, Discrimination, Harassment), oriented, standardized on the control group and inverse-covariance weighted as above.  Respondents in the Akbayan municipalities; assignment with city fixed effects, attendance weights, standard errors clustered by barangay (p = 0.032).  The main text reports this as the town-hall effect on awareness of gender-related issues (Figure 5, upper panel).

i4r.notes: Team-level verdict.  Database row "appendix table c.4, panel 1, column 1" (o_coeff 0.45, o_p 0.032), remove weights: r_coeff -0.001 (SE 0.036, p = 0.977) — the gender-index effect vanishes unweighted; not transcribed.

recomputed.notes: Outside tolerance: reproduced=0.36288 vs claimed=0.45 (relative error 19.36%, tolerance 2.00%).

ground_truth.unit: percentage points (probability of voting for the treating party list)
ground_truth.location: SI Table F.1, column 2 (Vote (Overall)), ITT row
ground_truth.context: SI Table F.1 ("ITT Effect and CACE on Electoral Returns at the Individual Level (Unweighted Results)"), column 2: the robustness version of the individual-level vote-choice ITT WITHOUT the attendance-oversampling adjustment (so self-reported attendees are overrepresented).  Outcome: survey respondent reports voting for the party list that campaigned in their municipality, in percent, among respondents who turned out, both party lists pooled.  Linear probability model on treatment assignment with city fixed effects; inference for the ITT under randomization of the treatment (permutation p = 0.00001).  Imus, Pateros and Santa Maria not included.

i4r.notes: Team-level verdict.  Database row "appendix table f.2" (= Table F.1 column 2; o_coeff recorded as 0.234 against the printed 23.242, i.e. 0.232 as a proportion — a transcription slip in the database; o_p 0.000), include omitted cities: r_coeff 0.235 (SE 0.052), not transcribed.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: Gender items oriented substantively (higher = more pro-gender-equality): equality and harassment kept as coded (5 = disagree with sexist statement), discrimination reversed (6 - x, higher = agree women lose jobs to discrimination), femhouse and fempol kept as coded (1/0). The paper's 'positive direction implies more agreement' is ambiguous for the gender items.
Poverty items: poverty, gap, corruption reversed (6 - x) so higher = more agreement; cct kept as coded.

Attendance weights constructed from the paper's description: in barangays where meetings were held (treatment == 1), attendees weighted att.prop / survey attendance share and non-attendees (1 - att.prop) / (1 - survey share); all other respondents (and respondents with missing attendance) weight 1.

Anderson indices: items standardized on the (unweighted) control-assignment group of the party's municipalities, inverse-covariance weights from the pairwise-complete covariance of standardized items, index averaged over non-missing items and re-standardized on the control group.
Individual analyses restricted to the 1,082 respondents with a valid party-list turnout answer; vote outcomes among respondents who turned out (turnout_pl == 1).
Permutation p-values not computed (only point estimates and counts requested).
cell.notes: Table 1: OLS of turnout.party / share.treated / share.akbayan / share.umalabka on assignment with city FE using all 39 barangay rows of data_agg (18 Akbayan, 21 Umalab Ka). Tables C.3/C.4: weighted OLS of Anderson summary index on assignment with city FE, clustered by barangay, by party list. Table F.1: unweighted LPM (x100) of vote / vote.akbayan on assignment with city FE among respondents who turned out. One exploratory run (attempt-1, no RESULT lines) inspected the data. Survey barangay names matched data_agg for every treated barangay present in the survey (Anabu II-F, San Rosario-Silangan, Tungkod have no survey respondents). No runs hung.
